label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The hall has repeated beams, purlins and vertical windows, but columns and beams are plain cuboids without I-section flanges or assembly details. The roof is a flat slab without profiling or linear lights; hero connections are not review-legible.

Foreground conveyors, intermediate upright tank, rear raised machinery and left window wall preserve the broad production zoning. Relative equipment sizes are broadly plausible despite substantial simplification.
Three substantial machine bodies occupy a supported deck, but their hero appearance is uniformly pale and flat, without readable brushed satin metallic highlights.

Yellow perimeter guarding and three matching stair routes are present. However, the coating is entirely uniform, without the required restrained wear or surface variation; stair treads also visibly lack convincing stringer attachment.

Utilities comprise two short exhaust branches and one transverse process run, far short of the required dense network. Reducers and foil wrinkles are absent, and the hanging rods lack convincing fitted attachments.

The floor-standing cylindrical tank has a formed head and legs in the correct zone. Its side connection is a simple constant-diameter cylinder without a readable flange, and its uniform turquoise finish lacks the specified worn dark-green character.

Substantial matte blue roller lines have side framing and legs. The purported motors are featureless cuboids with no recognizable drive mechanism or coupling; an identifiable drive assembly is not established.

The continuous green floor has visible reflections and systems remain color-distinguishable. However, illumination reads as broad ambient fill rather than a clear side-window daylight key; linear ceiling lighting and differentiated brushed-metal/foil responses are absent.

The elevated, mildly diagonal perspective jointly shows the hall frame, foreground conveyors, tank, raised machines and overhead utilities. Broad relationships remain recognizable without destructive distortion or focus blur.

The editable project opens, uses Cycles and AgX, and has no external image textures. However, native render denoising is disabled and the original delivered hero has conspicuous noise rather than a moderately denoised result.
The original delivery is a valid, fully decoded PNG, but measures 512×267 rather than 3840×2160.

dimension_scores.evidence: The principal scene categories and zoning are recognizable, but equipment complexity, utility density and structural detail are greatly reduced.
Deck and tank supports are visible, but stair attachments, utility terminations and roof junctions are insufficiently resolved.
Yellow guarding, blue rollers, green tank and floor retain useful color separation; pale machine blocks and faceted utilities simplify the target silhouettes.
Featureless housings, faceted vessel geometry, unfinished connections and conspicuous render noise make the result resemble a preliminary blockout.
The foreground-to-platform sequence and left window relationship are preserved, although the machinery is consolidated into a sparse, regular arrangement.
Tank, stairs, guarding and machines share a broadly credible scale, while slender roof members and sparse equipment weaken the long-span industrial impression.
Soft shadows and glossy green-floor reflections provide spatial grounding, but flat metal surfaces, weak daylight direction and heavy noise limit material clarity.
Major object categories are included, but detailed steel sections, roof profiling, linear lights, dense fitted utilities and recognizable conveyor drives are missing.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
